motion.name: ease-expo
motion.purpose: In-place physics: lifts, presses, arrow nudges, folder zoom, App Library. Exposed as --ease-expo and the Tailwind ease-out-expo utility.

motion.name: ease-native
motion.purpose: Navigation: the icon morph, the receding and advancing page, push and pop slides.

motion.name: press
motion.value: transform 300ms ease-expo; scale(0.9) icons, scale(0.95) Projects row icons, scale(0.98) linked widgets
motion.purpose: Tap physics on icons, folders, dock keys and linked widgets.

motion.name: lift
motion.value: transform 300ms ease-expo; translateY(-4px) icons, translateY(-2px) folders and Projects row icons
motion.purpose: Hover lift on home screen and dock icons.

motion.name: folder-zoom
motion.value: translate and scale 500ms ease-expo from the tile centre at scale(0.2); opacity 300ms
motion.purpose: Folder popover grows out of the tile it was opened from, via @starting-style and discrete display/overlay transitions.

motion.name: folder-scrim-fade
motion.purpose: Backdrop fade behind the folder panel.

motion.name: app-library-rise
motion.value: translate 24px to 0 and scale 0.96 to 1 over 450ms ease-expo; opacity 250ms; scrim 350ms
motion.purpose: The App Library popover slides up out of the phone dock; closes without animation before a page swap.

motion.name: vt-app-zoom
motion.value: group 500ms ease-native (exits 360ms); old image fades out 200ms ease-out (exits 240ms); new image fades in 350ms ease-native (exits 180ms ease-out)
motion.purpose: The single shared element (view-transition-name app-zoom): tapped icon to [data-zoom-target] sheet or dialog, and back to the icon, folder tile or dock key.

motion.name: vt-app-open-close
motion.value: root not animated; app-backdrop fades in 350ms ease-out, out 250ms ease-out
motion.purpose: Home screen to story dialog and back: the home screen stays still and keeps its scroll.

motion.name: vt-zoom-in
motion.value: old root recedes to scale 0.94, opacity 0.4, blur 2px over 450ms ease-native; new root fades in 300ms ease-native after 120ms
motion.purpose: An icon or dock key opens a section sheet.

motion.name: vt-zoom-out
motion.value: old root fades out 220ms ease-out; new root advances from scale 0.94, opacity 0.4, blur 2px over 450ms ease-native
motion.purpose: A sheet closes back to the home screen or another section.

motion.name: vt-push
motion.value: sheet-body: old slides to -24% and fades over 320ms, new slides in from 60% over 420ms, ease-native
motion.purpose: Deeper within one section (Blog list to post).

motion.name: vt-pop
motion.value: sheet-body: old slides to 60% and fades over 260ms, new slides in from -24% over 340ms, ease-native

motion.name: vt-chrome
motion.value: app-dock and status-bar groups and new images not animated, old images hidden
motion.purpose: Persisted dock and status bar never move during a page transition.

motion.name: color
motion.purpose: Colour and underline transitions on chips, rows, links and buttons.

motion.name: live-pulse
motion.purpose: The on-blue dot in the building-now widget.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: view transitions: groups not animated, 150ms crossfade, dock and status bar still; all other animation and transition durations 0.01ms
motion.purpose: prefers-reduced-motion: reduce removes movement and scaling everywhere.

narrative.overview:
The site is Dani's phone home screen laid flat on the web. The homepage is a grid of real things he made: native app icons pulled from each repository, language and npm glyph icons for the libraries without one, folders that zoom open out of their own tile, and widgets that hold who he is, what he is building now, and his photos. A dock pinned to the bottom of every page carries a Home key and the site sections as apps. Every inner page is an app opened from that screen: an app sheet with its section icon, an Archivo headline and a close button that returns home. Every catalog app opens as a story dialog over the home screen, the way a phone app opens on top of its springboard.

The world is calm and flat. A pale lavender wallpaper (deep ink at night) sits behind opaque white widgets with large, soft corners and no borders. Colour comes from the icons themselves, the section tints, a few flat bento tiles (yellow, pink, green) for stats and features, and one blue that means "live". Depth is tonal, not shadowed: the only cast shadow in the system belongs to the dock and the App Library that rises out of it. Density is high on the home screen (icons pack an 8-column grid) and generous inside sheets, where long-form reading gets a 68ch measure and 17px text.

The physics are a phone's: icons lift on hover and press down to 90% on tap, folders grow from the tile you touched, and navigation morphs the tapped icon into the sheet or dialog it opens and shrinks it back on close, while the dock and status bar hold still. In-place physics settle on an expo ease-out curve; navigation rides a slightly firmer native curve. The rejected alternatives were the long project list and the dark terminal portfolio; there is no glass, no gradient and no decorative shadow.
keyCharacteristics: Real app icons on the macOS squircle grid (22.5% corner radius, 9.6% inset margin), names set beneath.
Opaque, borderless widgets at a 1.75rem radius on a tinted wallpaper.
One blue for live state and actions; yellow, pink and green are bento tile fills; every other hue is an icon, a photo, or a section tint.
Archivo 800 with negative tracking for every heading, Hanken Grotesk for everything read.
A persisted dock and status bar on every page; inner pages are sheets and apps are dialogs, never a separate site chrome.
Navigation is spatial: icons zoom into sheets, apps open over a still home screen, list and detail push and pop sideways.
Light and dark ship together, switched by the status bar toggle and remembered per visitor.

rules.name: The One Blue Rule
rules.body: Blue means live or actionable: links, focus, selection, the building-now widget, the Active badge, the primary link in a story dialog. It never decorates. Yellow, pink and green are the bento tones that share the tile grid with it, but they mark a stat or feature tile, never state or an action.

rules.name: The Bento Tone Rule
rules.body: A bright bento tile is one flat fill with `on-bright` ink, used for a single stat or feature (stars, talks, newsletter). One tile per tone on a screen; never a bento tone as text, a link colour or an accent stripe.

rules.name: The Icon Owns Its Colour Rule
rules.body: Hue on the home screen comes from app icons, photos, section tints and the bento tiles. Neutrals stay in the 285 to 290 hue band and never compete.

rules.name: The Tint Is The Section Rule
rules.body: A section's tint and glyph appear together, everywhere that section is represented. Never recolour a section, and never borrow another section's tint for unrelated UI.

rules.name: The Heavy Headline Rule
rules.body: Every heading is Archivo at 800 with negative tracking between -0.02em and -0.03em, balanced with `text-wrap: balance`. Text below title size is always Hanken.

rules.name: The Ramp Only Rule
rules.body: Sizes come from the nine-step ramp (11, 12, 13, 15, 17, 20, 28, 44, 48px). Nothing is set in uppercase, and no letter-spaced small caps are used as section labels.

rules.name: The Tabular Time Rule
rules.body: Every `time` element and every count renders with tabular figures so dates and numbers align in columns.

rules.name: The Grid Is The Screen Rule
rules.body: Home screen content lives in grid cells, never in free-flowing sections. A new tool is a new icon or a folder entry, not a new block of prose.

rules.name: The Single Lift Rule
rules.body: Only the dock, and the App Library that opens out of it, casts a shadow. Everything else, including story dialogs, is lifted by tone and scrim.

rules.name: The Same Way Back Rule
rules.body: Whatever opened a view closes it in reverse: a sheet shrinks into the icon that opened it, a folder app returns into its folder tile, a section returns into its dock key.

rules.name: The Still Chrome Rule
rules.body: The dock and status bar are the phone's hardware. They never take part in a page transition.

dos: **Do** put every new tool, library or app on the home screen as an icon or inside a folder, using its real icon from its repository when one exists; otherwise a mark or glyph icon on the project's language or registry tint.
**Do** draw every non-native icon on the inset squircle (22.5% radius, 9.6% margin) so it aligns with downloaded app art.
**Do** record the provenance of every shipped raster or icon file (repository or Simple Icons version and licence).
**Do** open every inner page as an AppSheet with its section icon, h1 and close button, and keep the dock on every page.
**Do** open every catalog app as its story dialog over the home screen, with its outbound link as the single Live Blue button inside it.

**Do** use the expo ease (`cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)`) for lifts, presses, folder zooms and arrow nudges: 0.3s for presses and lifts, 0.5s for zooms. Use the native ease (`cubic-bezier(0.2, 0.9, 0.1, 1)`) for navigation, with exits faster than entrances.
**Do** mark a new page's main surface as the zoom target (`data-zoom-target`) and its tappable icon as the morph source, so navigation reads as one object moving.
**Do** put `on-bright` ink on every yellow, pink or green tile, and give inputs on a bright tile an `on-bright` focus ring.
**Do** give icons the press physics: lift on hover, scale to 0.9 on press; widgets that link press to 0.98.
**Do** keep touch targets at 36px minimum for chips and links and 40px for icon buttons.
**Do** design both themes together; at night, lift ink widgets and the dock above the card tone and rim icons so they do not sink.
**Do** let `prefers-reduced-motion` collapse every animation and transition (navigation becomes a 0.15s crossfade), and hide the status bar, dock and footer when printing.
donts: **Don't** add shadows to widgets, icons, sheets or dialogs; the dock and its App Library are the only surfaces that cast one.
**Don't** use glass, backdrop blur or gradients; the folder tile is a flat translucency and scrims are flat colour. The 2px blur on a receding page exists only for the length of a zoom transition.
**Don't** add borders to widgets; separate by tone, and keep hairlines for list rows and section rules.
**Don't** use blue for decoration; it is reserved for live state, links, focus and the primary action.
**Don't** use a bento tone (yellow, pink, green) for text, links, borders or state, or repeat one tone across tiles on the same screen.
**Don't** animate the dock or status bar between pages, or give a second element the `app-zoom` name.
**Don't** recolour a section's tint or pair a section glyph with another tint.
**Don't** set sizes outside the ramp or set labels in uppercase with letter-spacing.
**Don't** use emoji or text characters as icons; glyph icons are vector logo masks.
**Don't** invent catalog entries; an icon on the screen must be a real public repo or a package verified on the registry.
